title: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang Reveals Tiny AI Robots at GTC Berlin 2026

lines.text: So these tiny robots can walk, fall over and get right back up, and nobody programmed those moves step by step.

At NVIDIA's keynote in Berlin, Jensen Huang brought out four of them, little two-legged robots about twenty-five centimetres tall, and they walked, they tumbled, and when he told them to sit, stand or lie down, they actually did it.
lines.label: 25 CM

lines.text: Now each one has a camera, a laser that measures distance, motion sensors that feel every tilt and fifteen small motors, but that's not the clever part, the clever part is how they learned to move.
lines.label: 15 MOTORS

lines.text: Engineers let them practise thousands of times inside a simulation, and every time a robot got a step closer to the goal, it got a reward, so all that practice turns into one skill, and they carry that skill over to the real robot, and now it can walk, kick, grab, even pick itself up after a fall.
lines.label: PRACTICE

lines.text: But let's be honest, this was a stage demo, and if you change the floor or change the task, it can still lose its balance.
So what this really shows you is that experimenting with robots just got a lot cheaper, it doesn't mean robots got a human brain.
lines.label: CHEAPER

lines.text: And if you want the engineering behind every robot demo like this, follow the channel.
So would you trust one of these in your home, or is it just a lab toy?
